caption: TEG Dehydration: Effect of Circulation Rate on Water Content. CPA SimpleTEGAbsorber with explicit fixed-inventory energy reconstruction; 99.5 weight percent lean TEG, five stages and 70 percent stage efficiency.
title: TEG Dehydration: Effect of Circulation Rate on Water Content
observation: Dry-gas water decreases from 36.596 ppmv at 500 kg/hr circulation to a sampled minimum of 18.177 ppmv at 4181.8 kg/hr, then rises slightly to 18.195 ppmv at 5000 kg/hr. All reconstructed cases retain explicit material and energy checks.
mechanism: The CPA/Kremser approximation is rerun at each circulation rate, then a common outlet temperature closes the adiabatic energy balance while preserving its predicted component inventories. implication: The shallow minimum shows that more solvent does not guarantee a monotonically lower water content; the native contacting approximation is not a rigorous multistage energy model.
recommendation: Use the minimum as a screening observation, verify lean-solvent purity and thermal conditions, and calibrate contacting performance before selecting a field circulation rate.
